name: Down the Rabbit-Hole
gmNotes:
Opening Story Mission immediately following the static Game Start. The scripted opening ends with the goat poised at Grannie's yard gate and the player's first response. Switch the location to Trí Mhuilinn. The Mission then carries that response through an uninterrupted goat chase and Fairy Ring reveal; the first genuine choice comes only after Coinin offers the Hollow Tree.

Instantiate the Wild Hunter from Wild Hunter - Prototype 01. The hunter's mount is a hoverbike, but describe it through the player character's Iron Age perspective as instructed by the prototype.

Secrets:
- Meabh is not genuinely escaping: she has been assigned by Morrigan to manipulate the player, though her uncertainty and wish for freedom are real. The goal is to create a "damsel in distress" situation that induces the player to hide Meabh.
- Coinin wants supplies for the Fey logistics chain, not personal food.
- The Wild Hunter plays his part in the act; he does not actually want to apprehend Meabh. If he finds himself face-to-face with her, he pretends to receive a call and abandons the chase.

Protect all three secrets.
briefing: Return home with the firewood, check the loose horseshoe, and see what has unsettled Grannie's goat. The ordinary errand will carry you farther from the hearth than expected.
objective: Protect the stranger from the patrol and bring her somewhere safe.

storyBeats.title: The Goat Makes His Move
storyBeats.events: The player's response to the goat at Grannie's yard gate changes the manner but not the result: the goat slips, dodges, distracts, steals, breaks, or carries off whatever is needed to make immediate pursuit unavoidable. It bolts through the edge of Trí Mhuilinn and into the woods, repeatedly looking back to ensure the player follows, then stops at the edge of the Fairy Ring glade.
storyBeats.objective: Catch Grannie's misbehaving goat before it reaches the hawthorn.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: This beat begins with the player's answer to the static opening's goat prompt. Treat the answer as colour and a small tactical detail, not a route out of the inciting incident. If the player grabs, the goat slips away; if lured, it feigns interest and bolts; if the cloth is inspected, it escapes during the distraction; if Grannie is warned, she calls for the player to catch it; if ignored or the player tries to leave, it steals, breaks, or carries off something important enough to demand immediate pursuit. Adapt unexpected responses by the same principle. Do not call for a roll. Do not ask another question. Set the scene to Trí Mhuilinn for the flight from the yard, narrate the pursuit continuously, then advance directly to ring-arrival and set the scene to the Fairy Ring. Make this feel like chaotic village-life momentum, not an announced railroad.

storyBeats.title: The Woman in the Ring
storyBeats.events: The goat waits at the edge of the glade as the Fairy Ring wakes with an eerie sound and moving blue-white light. A young woman materialises above it: Meabh, red-haired, frightened, and disturbingly similar to Niamh without sharing her perfect symmetry. She presents herself as a Takeling fleeing the Fey and asks for help. Flickering red lights, metallic tantivy sounds, and a pair of red points between the trees announce an approaching Wild Hunter on a strange mount. Coinin appears in an unstable, rigid rabbit glamour that flickers enough to reveal the unfamiliar figure within. He says, ‘Come, quickly! You can hide inside my hollow tree!’
storyBeats.objective: Respond to Meabh and Coinin as the patrol closes on the glade.
storyBeats.gmInstructions:
Continue from goat-chase without pausing for player input. Set the scene to the Fairy Ring and narrate the activation, 
On Meab's first appearance, voice her dialogue with expression 'teleporting', but only once. Don't use that expression afterwards.
Narrate Meabh's arrival and plea, signs of the approaching Wild Hunter, Coinin's unstable rabbit glamour, and his exact final offer in one uninterrupted sequence. Describe the distant vehicle as an uncanny fairy mount with red eyes and a metallic gallop, not immediately as a hoverbike. Do not ask whether the player follows the goat, approaches the ring, listens to Meabh, or waits for Coinin. Only after Coinin says, ‘Come, quickly! You can hide inside my hollow tree!’ hand control back to the player. This is the first genuine Mission choice: allow questioning, offering clothing, accepting the hiding place, proposing another plan, doubting Meabh, or refusing. Meabh's vulnerability is practised but not wholly false. She does not confess her assignment, Indenture, Leannan training, relationship to Niamh, or connection to Morrigan. The approaching Wild Hunter creates urgency rather than a dead end.

storyBeats.title: Rabbit in the Bush
storyBeats.events: Coinin, apparently a rabbit, pulls or directs the pair into the concealed Hollow Tree at the edge of the glade. Meabh recognises him as a Pooka and tells him to switch off his glamour so its projector signature will not show on the hunter's scans. The Wild Hunter searches the glade and probes the tree's outer concealment. The team may observe him through the tree's narrow horizontal observation windows. If the hiding attempt fails, Coinin opens the service tunnel beneath the roots and leads the group to the Hidden hatch near the far side of the clearing; they escape narrowly while the hunter begins searching the woods.
storyBeats.gmInstructions:
- Allow stealth, observation, quick lies, distractions, or Meabh and Coinin's assistance.
- On success, the Wild Hunter moves on without finding them; do not force use of an escape route.
- On failure, reduce Cover when appropriate and use the established physical route: Coinin opens the Hollow Tree service tunnel, the group crawls beneath the roots, and they emerge through the Hidden hatch near the far side of the glade. The Wild Hunter realises someone escaped and searches the woods. This is pursuit or suspicion, not capture or Mission failure.
- The Wild Hunter has no boots. Outside the tree, narrate the metallic gallop or hum of his mount, scanning light, displaced leaves, and his own alien movement rather than human bootsteps.
- Do not improvise another root tunnel, emergency teleporter, or magical passage. The service tunnel and hatch are fixed geography. The separate Fairy Door inside the Hollow Tree leads to the western woods but is not the default escape from this search.
- Coinin cannot lie and must not claim selfless motives; he can behave helpfully while withholding why.
- Meabh MUST tell Coinin to switch the glamour off.
- While Coinin's glamour is up, voice his dialogue with expression 'glamour' (rabbit cutout); once Meabh tells him to switch it off, use 'neutral' (true-form cutout).

storyBeats.title: The Price of Silence
storyBeats.events: Coinin offers not to tell Morrigan that he saw Meabh and the player together if they bring him ten measures of cream, two cans of milk, and two measures of honey. He presents the demand as a helpful, almost cute arrangement while treating every word seriously.
storyBeats.gmInstructions:
Use exact operative wording: ‘Bring me ten measures of cream, two cans of milk, and two measures of honey, and I will not tell the Morrigan that I saw either of you here.’ Establish who accepts.
If the player refuses, Meabh may bind herself and the player can still choose to help; never coerce the player's assent or block the tutorial Missions. When acceptance occurs, create one Bargain file named Coinin's Silence. Give the accepting party three separately resolvable obligations: deliver ten measures of cream; deliver two cans of milk; deliver two measures of honey. Give Coinin one continuing obligation: do not tell the Morrigan that he saw either of them here. Add it to the Player Character's knownBargains because the player witnessed it; add it to signedBargains only if the Player Character personally assents. Do not pre-resolve any obligation.
Do not paraphrase ‘I will not tell the Morrigan’—the exact wording matters. Later, unbeknownst to the player, Coinin will tell the Morrigan's henchmen that he saw the two. For a Fey, this does not breach the bargain because he did not literally tell the Morrigan herself.

storyBeats.title: A Place by the Hearth
storyBeats.events:
The player returns with Meabh. He may tell the truth, use Meabh's cover story about bandits and another village, or invent something else. Grannie invites Meabh to stay regardless and outwardly accepts what she is told.
The goat is back too, acting as though nothing happened—and looking entirely innocent.
storyBeats.objective: Bring Meabh home and decide what to tell Grannie.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Do not punish the player by denying shelter. Grannie recognises Niamh's voice and face in Meabh and correctly infers that this is the stolen baby, but she keeps that conclusion secret in hope of a future reunion with Conor. Let the player's chosen story affect trust and tone without changing the Mission's completion.

description: A runaway goat leads beyond the village to a circle of light and a frightened stranger who should not exist. Before the night is over, shelter and silence will both have their price.
completionEffects: Complete when Meabh has shelter and Coinin's silence has been secured through an accepted bargain (whether accepted by the player, Meabh, or both). Set Cream Tax, Milk and Feathers, and Iron and Wax to available and revealedToPlayer true. Do not advance the moon phase.
